name: F1/87/88C
hook: In 1988 McLaren won fifteen of sixteen Grands Prix, and the one it lost went to a year-old Ferrari, at Monza, four weeks after Enzo Ferrari died.
story:
Picture Monza in September 1988. The grandstands are packed, and they are grieving.

Enzo Ferrari had died four weeks earlier. And that season, nobody could touch McLaren. Its cars had won every race so far.

Ferrari's car was a patched-up veteran. It was last year's design, with last year's turbo V6 reworked for tighter rules. It drank too much fuel. Ayrton Senna put his McLaren on pole. Gerhard Berger and Michele Alboreto lined up third and fourth.

Then the luck turned. Alain Prost's engine faltered, and he retired on lap 35. Senna kept leading. With two laps to go, he came up to lap a stand-in Williams driver, Jean-Louis Schlesser. Schlesser's brakes locked. The Williams ran wide, the cars touched, and Senna was out with broken suspension.

Berger inherited the lead and won. Alboreto came home second. A Ferrari one-two, at Monza, weeks after the old man's death.

It was the only race McLaren lost all year.
description: The F1/87/88C was Scuderia Ferrari's Formula One car for 1988, an update of the 1987 F1/87. Gustav Brunner led the design, with John Barnard as technical director. It used a carbon and Kevlar monocoque and the Tipo 033A, a 1,496 cc turbocharged V6 held to 2.5 bar of boost and 150 litres of fuel a race. Gerhard Berger and Michele Alboreto drove it. Its famous day was the 1988 Italian Grand Prix, where it finished first and second.
